leading_positions.synthesis: Six of eight members name B009 as their sole preferred configuration, each with Kane, Mele and Molenkamp. Several moved to it from other opening first choices (Eriksson from B014, Johansson from B010, Olsson from B033, Pearce from B024). What is shared is the trio and the theory-plus-experiment logic: the Z2 invariant and quantum spin Hall prediction, then the HgTe quantum-well observation. What is not shared is the citation wording. Danielsson and Eriksson favour a narrow citation around the quantum spin Hall state and Z2 topological insulators; Johansson, Mehlig, Olsson and Pearce specify prediction plus first realisation in HgTe quantum wells. Members also differ on how openly the omission of Bernevig-Hughes-Zhang and Hasan should be acknowledged, and on whether the 2D and 3D steps are one discovery or two. Several supporters name alternatives (B033, B037, B010, B024, B014, B045, B026) but these are not part of their preferred configuration.

Two members prefer Katori and Ye for optical lattice clocks as a single-part prize. They agree on a clean two-name attribution (concept and first demonstrations versus accuracy, stability and many-body control), maturity through independent laboratories, and concrete consequences such as a possible redefinition of the second. They also name B009 as an alternative. Both accept that separation from the 2005 frequency-comb and 2012 ion-control prizes must be argued explicitly in the citation, and both rely on recollection for magic-wavelength priority. Lindroth treats the overlap objection as answerable; Kroll treats it as the main risk and frames the dispute with B009 as partly one of timing and credit clarity.

areas_of_agreement: All eight members prefer a single-part prize, and no member proposed pairing two achievements.

The Kane-Mele Z2 prediction plus Molenkamp's HgTe observation is accepted by every member who discussed B009 as a genuine theory-plus-experiment discovery with about two decades of independent confirmation by transport, ARPES and STM.

Every member who addressed B009 names the Bernevig-Hughes-Zhang proposal and Hasan's three-dimensional work as a real attribution weakness that the three-name limit cannot cure; none claims the trio is uncontested.
Members who commented agree that B026 has the cleanest attribution on the shortlist and is mature, and that B010 raises a timing concern after the 2025 prize on superconducting circuits.

Members who discussed B014, B033 and B024 consider them unready or weakly attributed for this round (Metzner missing for B014; Andrei and an unsettled mechanism for B033; a single credited name for a very large collaboration for B024), though several keep B014 or B033 as alternatives or future candidates.
scientific_disputes: Whether the 2D quantum spin Hall step and the 3D topological insulator work are one discovery or two: Eriksson separates them; Danielsson, Mehlig and Olsson treat the 3D step as a possible different, larger prize.

Whether B009 is a distinct step beyond the 2016 prize on topological phase transitions and phases of matter (Olsson, Pearce and Eriksson say yes; Kroll and Danielsson raise the incrementalism objection; Johansson says some members may see a continuation).

Whether lattice clocks are a distinct discovery or a refinement of precision metrology already covered by the 2005 comb and 2012 ion-control prizes (Lindroth: distinct; Kroll, Danielsson, Eriksson, Johansson and Olsson: a real question).

Whether quantum simulation with ultracold atoms (B037) is a discovery in its own right and whether its theory origin in Jaksch-Zoller should shape the trio (Lindroth and Johansson disagree on experimental-only versus theory-inclusive credit).
attribution_disputes: B009: whether Mele, Hasan or the Bernevig-Hughes-Zhang proposers should hold the third slot; Danielsson, Olsson and Johansson keep Mele because the Z2 invariant underlies both the HgTe and 3D work, while Mehlig, Johansson and Eriksson say any omission should be stated openly.
B026: priority for the magic-wavelength proposal and the claims of other neutral-atom and ion-clock groups are unverified in the materials and rest on recollection.
B014: Metzner is outside the credited names, so Georges, Vollhardt and Kotliar do not match the intellectual history; Eriksson concedes this and Johansson asks whether it is any easier than for B009.
B033: Andrei's early STM evidence is outside a Bistritzer-MacDonald-Jarillo-Herrero trio.
B024: only Halzen is credited for a result produced by a very large collaboration; no member has identified a defensible partner or conception credit within the shortlist.
B037 and B030: Zoller and Cirac recur across candidates, so a prize on one would affect the other; the proposed trios for B037 also differ (Greiner, Esslinger, Zoller or Cirac).
maturity_disputes: B033 is under ten years old as an experimental field with the superconducting mechanism unsettled; Danielsson, Eriksson, Johansson, Lindroth, Mehlig and Olsson treat it as a likely later prize, while Olsson argues the discovery of the phases is secure regardless of mechanism.
B024: the diffuse neutrino flux is secure while source identification is only partial (Danielsson), which some see as a maturity limit alongside the attribution problem.

B010 sits close to the 2025 prize; Lindroth and Kroll see this as a reason to wait, Johansson as a reason not to press her own first choice, while Pearce asks whether it is disqualifying or only a delay.
B009 is two decades old and stably interpreted, which supporters cite as a maturity advantage over B033, while Kroll holds that its novelty is partly spent after 2016.
conflict_or_recusal_flags: Johansson: professor at Chalmers and director of WACQT, working on circuit and waveguide QED; Chalmers colleagues Delsing and Wilson work in the same area. She ranked B010 first and states she should recuse or disclose if B010 is decided against other candidates. No connection to B009 names is apparent.

Kroll: documented research stay in John Hall's laboratory in Boulder; Hall's comb work is linked to the history of B026 and the group around Jun Ye, though no collaboration with Katori or Ye is documented. He also took part in WACQT management, relevant to B010. He flags this for recusal discussion on B026.
Lindroth: field proximity to atomic and optical candidates B026, B037 and B030, disclosed as scientific closeness with no personal tie to credited names.
Eriksson: professional interest in DMFT (B014) through DFT+DMFT work, with no documented tie to Georges, Kotliar or Vollhardt; B014 is only an alternative.
Pearce (chair): proximity to astroparticle physics (B024, IceCube) with no documented tie to IceCube or Halzen; B024 is only an alternative in the chair's own ballot.
Olsson notes that her Chalmers colleague Johansson works in the circuit QED field relevant to B010, which she has not proposed.
Danielsson and Mehlig report no apparent conflict.
questions_for_round2: For B009, should the committee settle the 2D versus 3D question explicitly, and if the citation is limited to the quantum spin Hall state and its HgTe realisation, how should the text acknowledge the Bernevig-Hughes-Zhang proposal and Hasan without implying credit the trio cannot carry?
Is the third B009 slot defensible as Mele rather than Hasan, and would any member change position if it were Hasan?
Is B009 a distinct advance beyond the 2016 prize, and what specific difference between band topology of real insulators and the earlier work should the citation state?

For B026, what distinguishes lattice clocks from the 2005 frequency-comb and 2012 ion-control prizes, and can magic-wavelength priority and the claims of other lattice-clock and ion-clock groups be verified from the materials supplied?

Do Kroll and Lindroth treat B009 as an acceptable compromise if B026 does not carry, and do the six B009 supporters see B026 as an acceptable alternative, or does the clean credit boundary change any ranking?
Does the 2025 prize on superconducting circuits make B010 ineligible this year or only a timing question, and should Johansson recuse from any deliberation between B010 and other candidates?
Can the B024 credit be resolved with names beyond Halzen, and if not, does that settle the committee's position on IceCube for this year?
Should B033 be deferred on maturity grounds, or does the security of the observed phases justify considering it now despite Andrei's omission and the unsettled mechanism?
summary.chair_observation: The explicit round-1 configurations show six members on B009 (Kane, Mele, Molenkamp) and two on B026 (Katori, Ye), with no other shortlisted candidate preferred by any member. Both positions are acknowledged as strong; the main divide is between breadth of support and a conceptually deep but contested credit allocation in B009, versus a clean credit boundary and narrower support in B026. The B009 supporters differ on citation wording and on how to acknowledge omitted claimants, and the B026 supporters on how to separate it from earlier prizes. Support breadth is noted as a count, not as evidence of merit, and round 2 should test the remaining credit and novelty objections rather than rely on the count.
